description: 18a + 18b — Two-pronged structural test of the κ residual and cyFlQ's Δm formula. 18a: confirmed κ from Gram-det is exactly S-even (κ(q_0) = κ(1/q_0) at 100 dps), so the missing 0.166 cannot come from this formula. 18b: cyFlQ's schematic Δm = 2·m_e·8G·H_A²·Φ_3(β_p) gives 0.205 MeV vs CODATA 1.293 MeV — short by factor 6.31. The closest S-even multiplier is 2π (off 0.45%) — same near-miss pattern as the κ residual's 1/6 (off 0.31%).

test_18a_kappa_S_eigenvalue.verdict: S-EVEN_BY_CONSTRUCTION — every [n]_q is palindromic in q so the Gram-det formula has no S-odd component. The missing 0.166 to close 1/α requires an S-odd structural term outside the J²-jet Gram, consistent with cyFlQ Lemma 6.4 (chirality channel Φ_3 is the unique S-odd carrier in the Wedderburn formula).

structural_pattern: Both κ-residual (1/6, 0.31% off) and Δm-residual (2π, 0.45% off) show the SAME pattern: a phenomenological residual that ALMOST matches a simple closed form but resists exact identification at 25-digit PSLQ. This consistently appears at the structural floor of the framework's α/Δm work — the same depth at which cyFlQ's PSLQ analysis falsified all simple closed forms for α*.
interpretation: All four high-precision attempts to close α/Δm/np from (q_0, m_e) alone — T1.1 (m_e·Σ_3), 14a/b (Gram-det κ), 18b (2αH_A²Φ_3), cyFlQ α* — converge on the same structural floor: an S-odd residual that PSLQ cannot identify as a simple closed form. The framework's S-eigenvalue decomposition (cyFlQ Lemma 6.4) explicitly says S-odd contributions live in Φ_3 (chirality), but the EXACT prefactor for Φ_3 in Δm has not been identified. This is plausibly the framework's deepest open structural question for nucleon mass.
next_steps: PSLQ at 50-100 dps on the 6.31× multiplier with extended basis (q, h_q, π, ζ(3), Apéry).
Search for the structural form 'X · α · H_A² · Φ_3' where X is a known invariant of Bring's surface (Reidemeister torsion, Maslov index, S³_q volume).
Check whether (Δm_codata + Δ_correction) where Δ_correction is the unaccounted 0.17% from F.1 closes the gap exactly; this would unify the F.1 finding with the 18b finding.
